name: Visbreaking and solvent deasphalting
principle: Visbreaking mildly thermally cracks vacuum residue to cut its viscosity so less cutter stock is needed for fuel oil. Solvent deasphalting extracts deasphalted oil (DAO) from residue with a light hydrocarbon solvent, leaving asphaltenes or pitch; KBR's ROSE uses supercritical solvent recovery. DAO feeds FCC, hydrocrackers or lube plants.

process_steps.name: DAO to FCC, hydrocracker or lube plant
Asphaltenes to fuel oil, asphalt, coker, POX or pellets

key_equipment: extractor with Lubemax (trays) or Rosemax (packing) internals

performance.metric: DAO yield increase from Rosemax internals
performance.basis: KBR article claim, at maximum extraction; Rosemax 20 to 30% more capacity than random packing

source.note: PTQ / Digital Refining, Processing heavy ends Part II (KBR ROSE)

performance.metric: coke make reduction when coking ROSE asphaltenes instead of vacuum residue

source.note: PTQ / Digital Refining, Processing heavy ends Part II (KBR ROSE)

performance.unit: % conversion of residuum to naphtha (typical), giving about a five-fold viscosity reduction; 360-510 C cut yield 16-24% on feed depending on severity
performance.basis: Speight (2012): "A 5%-10% conversion of residuum to naphtha is usually sufficient to afford at least an approximate five-fold reduction in viscosity"; Stratiev et al. (Luko Neftochim): the unit objective is maximum vacuum-residue conversion with a stable residual fuel oil - higher furnace outlet temperature raises conversion but degrades colloidal stability (S-value), which sets the stability limit; 360-510 C cut yield 16-24% on feed depending on conversion

source.note: Speight, Visbreaking chapter (2012) PDF mirror; Stratiev et al. visbreaker residue papers on ResearchGate (read 2026-10-28)

advantages: DAO is a cleaner feed for downstream conversion
limitations: The article does not describe visbreaking process conditions or yields

sources.note: PTQ / Digital Refining, Processing heavy ends Part II (KBR ROSE)
